title: J.P. Morgan lifts 2026-end target for S&P 500 to 8,000 on AI, earnings strength
key_facts: J.P. Morgan raised its year-end S&P 500 target to 8,000 from 7,800 on Monday (5 Oct 2026).
The new target implies about 3.1% upside from the index's last close of 7,757.64.
At least seven brokerages now expect the benchmark to reach 8,000 by end-2026.
J.P. Morgan raised its 2026 S&P 500 earnings-per-share forecast to US$365 (from US$350) and its 2027 forecast to US$420 (from US$390).
Of 436 S&P 500 companies that had reported June-quarter results, 85.1% beat expectations (LSEG data), against a long-term average of 68% since 1994.
J.P. Morgan kept its forward valuation multiple at about 20 times, citing higher interest rates, geopolitical risks and heavy equity and debt issuance.
The S&P 500 has gained 13.3% so far this year.
quote_evidence: As elevated backlogs convert into recognized revenue, cloud growth should remain well supported, helping validate rising AI capex, strengthen order coverage, and further ease ROIC (return on invested capital) concerns.
why_it_matters_hint: A bank's forecast for the S&P 500 rests on earnings and AI spending; the call was made on Monday 5 Oct, so it is older news.
